captions.instagram:
How does homeopathy work?

Dilute a remedy 1 in 100, shake it, and repeat thirty times. Count the molecules with Avogadro's number, watch them run out at 12C, find out why 30C would need 10¹⁵ oceans to hold one, then run a fair test against a dummy pill.

→ In 1790 a German doctor, Samuel Hahnemann, took cinchona bark while healthy to see what it did.
→ Doctors then drained blood and gave mercury purges. His gentler method spread fast, including to India.
→ Homeopathy teaches "like cures like": onion makes eyes stream, so onion is its remedy for streaming colds.
→ Each step keeps 1 drop in 100 and shakes it hard. By 12C the substance has almost certainly gone.
→ To expect one molecule of a 30C remedy you would need about 10¹⁵ Earths' worth of ocean.

youtubeLong.description:
Dilute a remedy 1 in 100, shake it, and repeat thirty times. Count the molecules with Avogadro's number, watch them run out at 12C, find out why 30C would need 10¹⁵ oceans to hold one, then run a fair test against a dummy pill.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox-production-fd52.up.railway.app/e/homeopathyclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/homeopathyclear

In this video:
• A gentler medicine, from 1790. Samuel Hahnemann took cinchona bark while healthy, felt fever-like symptoms, and built homeopathy on it.
• Like cures like, as homeopathy describes it. Homeopathy teaches that a substance that causes symptoms in a healthy person, found in "provings", treats similar symptoms in the sick.
• Dilute and shake until nothing is left. Each C step is 1 part in 100 with hard shaking.
• From plant to sugar pill. A mother tincture is plant material soaked in alcohol.
• What fair tests show. Many people get better anyway, and people visit healers on their worst days.
• Use it wisely. The pills themselves carry little risk; delaying real treatment does.
